@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", HOSTILE_NAMES)
async def test_the_import_toast_paints_a_hostile_card_name_literally(
    name, mock_app_instance, monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """Frame slice B2b (AC#7): a real import of a card named like markup, beside
    a draft, so the import lands without auto-select and its toast names the
    card (spec 1.4.6, R33): ``Imported <name> · in Characters``, painted as
    typed and inert."""
    import json

    from textual.widgets import Input

    from Tests.UI.roleplay_frame_harness import fake_file_picker
    from Tests.UI.roleplay_import_fixtures import card_v2

    card = tmp_path / "hostile.json"
    card.write_text(json.dumps(card_v2(name)), encoding="utf-8")
    db = CharactersRAGDB(tmp_path / "hostile_import.db", "test-client")
    db.add_character_card({"name": "Abel Host", "description": "seed"})
    fake_file_picker(monkeypatch, card)
    try:
        async with open_styled_roleplay(
            "mock",
            mock_app_instance,
            size=SIZE,
            app_class=_RecordingStyledApp,
            character_db=db,
            notifications=True,
        ) as pilot:
            screen = pilot.app.screen
            await start_new(pilot)
            await wait_until(
                pilot, lambda: screen._edit_mode == "create", what="the draft"
            )
            draft = screen.query_one("#personas-char-editor-name", Input)
            draft.focus()
            await pilot.press(*"Draft Hero")
            await wait_until(
                pilot, lambda: screen.state.has_unsaved_changes, what="the dirty draft"
            )
            assert await pilot.click("#personas-library-import")
            toast = f"Imported {name} · in Characters"
            await wait_until(
                pilot,
                lambda: any(toast in row for row in painted_rows(screen)),
                what="the painted toast",
            )
            assert name in [row["name"] for row in db.list_character_cards()]
            # The toast is the only copy: the draft keeps the screen.
            await _assert_literal_and_inert(pilot, name, at_least=1)
            assert screen._edit_mode == "create"
    finally:
        db.close_connection()
```

# ---- Where an import lands (frame slice B2b, spec 1.4.6) ----

#: The workbench mode that lists each kind (``KIND_FOR_MODE`` reversed).
MODE_FOR_KIND: dict[str, str] = {kind: mode for mode, kind in KIND_FOR_MODE.items()}


def import_landing(
    *, clean: bool, intent_current: bool, presentation_current: bool
) -> Literal["select", "toast"]:
    """Whether an import that landed is selected, or only named in a toast.

    Quick import is kept: the new item is selected (in its own kind, which
    the screen switches to) only when nothing can be lost or overridden.

    Args:
        clean: Every Roleplay draft is clean (R24's aggregate predicate).
        intent_current: No newer intent (a kind switch, a create, a load, a
            cursor move) arrived since the picker opened.
        presentation_current: The screen still shows (attached, on top).

    Returns:
        ``"select"`` when all three hold, else ``"toast"``.
    """
    if clean and intent_current and presentation_current:
        return "select"
    return "toast"


def import_landed_toast(name: str, kind: str, *, existed: bool = False) -> str:
    """R33's literal copy for where an import went: ``Imported <name> · in <Kind>``.

    The screen paints it with markup off, so ``name`` goes in as typed (on
    one line).

    Args:
        name: The imported item's name.
        kind: Its entity kind (``ITEM_KINDS`` keys).
        existed: A character card that was already in the library (the
            importer returned the existing one).

    Returns:
        The toast text.
    """
    head = (
        f"{_one_line(name)} already existed"
        if existed
        else f"Imported {_one_line(name)}"
    )
    return f"{head} {resolve_glyph(_SEPARATOR)} in {ITEM_KINDS[kind][2]}"
```

        )

    def _bump_import_intent(self) -> None:
        """A newer user intent: an import in flight no longer auto-selects."""
        self._import_intent += 1

    def _import_intent_now(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """The user's intent so far: screen transitions and list cursor moves."""
        return self._import_intent, self._window_state.moves

    def _import_presentation_is_current(self, kind: str) -> bool:
        """Whether the screen still shows, so a landing may select (any kind)."""
        return bool(
            not self._closed
            and self._parent is not None
            and self.is_attached
            and self.app.screen is self
            and (kind != "character" or self._local_character_actions_allowed())
        )

    async def _land_import(
        self, kind: str, item_id: str, name: str, intent: tuple[int, int]
    ) -> bool:
        """Select an import where it landed, when nothing is lost (spec 1.4.6).

        Auto-select runs only when every Roleplay draft is clean (R24's
        aggregate, broader than ``_run_guarded``'s test: it also counts
        in-flight saves and staged attachments), no newer intent arrived since
        the picker opened, and the screen still shows; a clean import of
        another kind switches to that kind first. Otherwise the caller's
        literal toast names where it went. On dev a character import
        auto-selected whenever Characters showed (a draft started during the
        import was replaced from view, survey PROBE2), lore and dictionary
        imports whenever their kind showed, and a character import that
        landed after a kind switch said nothing (PROBE3).

        Args:
            kind: ``character``, ``lore`` or ``dictionary``.
            item_id: The imported item's id.
            name: Its name.
            intent: ``_import_intent_now()`` when the picker opened.

        Returns:
            True when the item was selected.
        """
        landing = frame_state.import_landing(
            clean=self._aggregate_roleplay_draft_snapshot().is_clean,
            intent_current=self._import_intent_now() == intent,
            presentation_current=self._import_presentation_is_current(kind),
        )
        if landing != "select":
            return False
        mode = frame_state.MODE_FOR_KIND[kind]

        async def select() -> None:
            if self.state.active_mode != mode:
                # Clean, so no draft is asked about; the new kind's list
                # starts unfiltered.
                await self._apply_mode(mode)
            else:
                # Clear an active search so the imported row is in the list.
                self._cancel_search_debounce()
                self.state.search_query = ""
                try:
                    self.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input).value = ""
                except Exception:
                    pass
                if kind == "character":
                    if self.state.sort_key == "relevance":
                        self.state.sort_key = "name_asc"
                    await self.character_handler.refresh_character_list()
                elif kind == "lore":
                    await self._render_lore_rows(query="")
                else:

### Task 6: The J1 journey: import a PNG card, then a strict xfail for Chat now (spec §5.7.3, AC#15, AC#4's PNG end to end)

**Why.** Spec §5.7.3 asks for journey J1, "import a PNG card and chat with it", in the B1 journey form (RC-7): a passing prefix test of the steps delivered so far, and a full-journey test marked `xfail(strict=True, raises=NotYetDelivered)` whose undelivered steps each raise `NotYetDelivered`. Tasks 4 and 5 delivered the import half: the one picker routes a PNG card to Characters and the guarded landing selects it when nothing is dirty. Chat now from the loaded card belongs to frame slice B5b-2 and the provider request to B5c. Those two owners are taken from the outline's row order; the spec does not name them, so they are an assumption the plan review checks.

The prefix also passes on dev today: dev's Characters picker already imported a PNG card and selected it (measured in a scratch tree at `38623632e9` with the journeys file, the harness and the fixtures copied in). So this task adds no behaviour. It pins dev's quick import as it now runs through B2b's one picker and guarded landing, and its reds are the two named mutations: the landing never selecting (M6-A) and the loaded row no longer painting its glyph (M6-B).

The loaded-row check reads the painted prompt's gutter (`▸` before the name), not only `item_at(...).active`. That is the B2a carry-over's rule (painted, not row data): M6-B leaves `row.active` true while the glyph is gone, and only the painted check sees it. The full journey's undelivered steps sit before the Chat now click, so the strict xfail raises `NotYetDelivered` as soon as the delivered prefix passes. A regression in the prefix fails it with an `AssertionError` instead, which strict mode reports as a failure (M6-A shows both tests red).

**Files:**
- Modify: `Tests/UI/test_roleplay_journeys.py` (the module docstring; the `fake_file_picker`, `item_at` and `png_card_bytes` imports; `J1_CARD`, the `j1_db` fixture, the `_import_the_png_card` helper and the two J1 tests).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes from Task 3: `Tests/UI/roleplay_import_fixtures.png_card_bytes(card: dict | None = None) -> bytes` (a PNG with a `chara` tEXt chunk; its default card is named "Wren Halloway").

- Consumes from B1 and B2a: `roleplay_full_app(*, size: tuple[int, int], entry: str = "initial_tab", ascii_glyphs: bool = False, notifications: bool = False, on_home: Callable[[Any], None] | None = None, character_db: CharactersRAGDB | None = None)` (async context manager yielding a pilot), `item_at(node, index: int | str) -> RoleplayItemView` (`.active`, `.name`), `settle(pilot)`, `wait_until(pilot, predicate, *, what)`, `not_yet_delivered(step: str, owner: str) -> None` and `NotYetDelivered`.

# ---- J1: import a PNG card, then chat with it (frame slice B2b; spec 5.7.3) ----

#: The PNG fixture's card name (Tests/UI/roleplay_import_fixtures.py).
J1_CARD = "Wren Halloway"


@pytest.fixture
def j1_db(tmp_path):
    """A file-backed ChaChaNotes with one character (the list needs a first row)."""
    db = CharactersRAGDB(tmp_path / "j1.db", "roleplay-journey-j1")
    db.add_character_card({"name": "Abel Host", "description": "seed"})
    yield db
    db.close_connection()


async def _import_the_png_card(pilot, monkeypatch, tmp_path) -> str:
    """Import (the one picker answers with a PNG card), then wait for it to load.

    Returns:
        The imported card's option id.
    """
    card = tmp_path / "wren.png"
    card.write_bytes(png_card_bytes())
    fake_file_picker(monkeypatch, card)
    screen = pilot.app.screen
    assert await pilot.click("#personas-library-import")
    await wait_until(
        pilot,
        lambda: screen.state.selected_entity_name == J1_CARD,
        what="the imported card loaded",
    )
    await settle(pilot)
    return f"character:{screen.state.selected_entity_id}"


async def test_j1_prefix_import_a_png_card_selects_and_loads_it(
    j1_db, monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """J1's delivered steps on the real app: Import, the PNG card through the
    one picker, then its row is the loaded one (the gutter's loaded glyph),
    its card shows, and the database holds it."""
    async with roleplay_full_app(size=(120, 36), character_db=j1_db) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        option_id = await _import_the_png_card(pilot, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
        row = item_at(screen, option_id)
        assert row.active and row.name == J1_CARD
        prompt = screen.query_one("#personas-library-rows").get_option(option_id).prompt
        assert "▸" in prompt.plain.split(J1_CARD)[0]
        card_name = screen.query_one("#personas-character-card-name", Static)
        assert str(card_name.render()) == f"Name: {J1_CARD}"
        stored = j1_db.get_character_card_by_name(J1_CARD)
        assert stored is not None
        assert option_id == f"character:{stored['id']}"


@pytest.mark.xfail(
    strict=True,
    raises=NotYetDelivered,
    reason="J1: Chat now from the card is frame slice B5b-2's, the request B5c's",
)
async def test_j1_full_journey_import_png_chat_now_provider_received_one_request(
    j1_db, monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """Import a PNG card, Chat now, and the provider receives one request
    (spec 5.7.3). Every undelivered step raises ``NotYetDelivered``; the slice
    that delivers a step replaces its raise with the step."""
    async with roleplay_full_app(size=(120, 36), character_db=j1_db) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        await _import_the_png_card(pilot, monkeypatch, tmp_path)
        not_yet_delivered("Chat now from the loaded card", "B5b-2")
        assert await pilot.click("#personas-start-chat")
        not_yet_delivered("the provider received one request", "B5c")

### Task 7: The one-row items toolbar; the old toolbar's 2 broad rules leave and the ratchet is lowered (spec §1.5.1, §5.3, §2.12 item 1, owner decision D2; RP-008, RP-009; AC#1, AC#2, AC#14, AC#19-#23)

**Why.** On dev today the items toolbar stacks one button per row at every design size, so the first item sits on row 19 at 120x36 and at 160x45 (row 18 at 80x24). Since Task 4 the branch's stacked toolbar holds only `+ New` and Import, with Sort and Tag on a second bar, and the first item sits on row 16 at 120x36 (the interim band Tasks 1, 2 and 4 pinned by measurement). Focusing dev's one-row search box adds an `Input:focus` border that leaves the box no content row: typed text is invisible and the list drops a row (RP-009, TASK-33787). Both exist on dev, and this task fixes both.

The search becomes the boot dense-form input, `.settings-compact-input`, which is one row at rest and focused. Beside it sit `Name` (the sort), `Tag` and `+ New`, which take the row under it at 120 columns and stack one per row only at 80x24. Owner decision D2 puts the interim `Import…` on the rail's title row beside "Library" until frame slice B6's rail takes it; "Library" yields below about 100 columns. The first item then sits on row 13 at 120 columns (band 8 under the header), on row 12 at 160 and wider (band 7) and on row 14 at 80x24 (band 9). At 120x36, 20 characters show where AC#2 asks for at least 19; B2a's stacked toolbar left room for 14 (it pinned 13).

`roleplay_frame_state.fit_items_toolbar` is the one owner of every word the toolbar paints. It is a ladder: one row with the full labels, one row with the short labels, two rows (full, then short), and finally one control per row. The search keeps at least `TOOLBAR_SEARCH_MIN_CELLS = 14` cells beside the controls, and shows its long placeholder ("Search characters…") only where it fits. `PersonasLibraryPane._apply_toolbar_fit` applies a fit by display alone (two classes, the labels and one inline width per control) and does nothing when the fit equals the one applied, so a resize mounts nothing (spec §2.13).

The old toolbar's `BUNDLED_CSS` held 4 rules, 2 of them counted by the broad-selector ratchet (`#personas-library-toolbar Button, …filterbar Button` and the stacked-controls pair). They leave, the ratchet is lowered from 270 to 267 on `2ee6f1a473`, the measurement (spec §2.12 item 1, AC#14; dev's own count fell to 269 after `38623632e9`, so the dry run's 268 would leave 1 of slack), and the `PersonasLibraryPane` boot segment shrinks from 923 B to 565 B (the gate: it must not grow).

Rulings the dry run made, each listed for the plan review:
- `fit_items_toolbar(mode, *, width, sort_key)` drops the outline's `server` parameter. The server's own order is `sort_key=SERVER_SORT_KEY` ("Server order", short "Server"): one input per fact.
- `ToolbarFit` gains `title` (D2), and its `labels` carry `search` (the placeholder the fit chose) and `import`.
- Short sort labels: "Best" (Relevance), "Name", "Edited", "Added", "Server". At 160 columns (35 cells) a Characters list sorted by Recent edit or Server order shows the short label so the toolbar stays one row: spec §1.5.1 allows it ("labels shorten, never wrap"), but owner decision D2 said "Full labels", so it is a recorded deviation from D2's wording (plan review ruling 6; Q7, accepted with the owner's agreement, 2026-10-29); the tooltip names the sort in full. Placeholders: "Search characters…", "Search personas…", "Search lore books…", "Search chat dictionaries…", short "Search…"; no `/` hint until frame slice B3 binds the key (D4). Tooltips: "Sort: <full>. Click to change the order. (s)"; Tag "Filter characters by tag." or "A tag narrows the list (named in its title). Pick All to clear it." The owner sees them in Task 14's captures.
- The controls are compact Buttons exactly their label wide (an inline width with a `ds-runtime` marker and `line_pad` 0, the marks bar's precedent), with a 1-cell margin as the gap. Textual 8.2.8 pads an auto-width Button by two cells and refuses `line-pad: 0` in CSS: a Textual limitation that exists on dev too, which B2b works around and does not fix.
- A harness fallback stays in `BUNDLED_CSS`: 5 rules, 565 B, id and class subjects only, under dev's 923 B segment. Without it the unstyled tier (`PersonasTestApp`, `ConsolidatedCSSApp` hosts) pushes the controls out of the pane: probe P7-1 measured 4 and then 23 unstyled tests that could not click Import or `+ New`. The app's lazy rules win wherever both load.
- The search keeps the id `#personas-library-search` (a spec deviation from `#personas-filter`, which the outline lists) and reuses `.settings-compact-input`, so it adds no focus edge and no boot bytes.
- The RP-009 and whole-and-inside tests loop the 4 kinds inside one mount per size (3 and 4 mounts instead of 12 and 16) to save lane minutes; a failure names the kind in its message rather than in the node id.
- The band test keeps 80x24 (band 9, the stacked controls) besides the outline's three sizes, because the old test covered it.
- The PS row is lowered to the measurement (17,118 → 17,108), as Task 4 lowered the pane's row (spec §5.4 item 4).

Finding M7-H (exists on dev, not fixed by B2b): the sort and tag legs of the shared-mode ownership tests in `test_personas_workbench.py` cannot see a stale sort or tag publication, because the newer owner stamps after the stale render in every ordering they build. They stay green under M7-H on the branch and, with dev's label API, on Task 6's tree. Their row legs still discriminate, so they are re-pinned faithfully; Task 15 files the follow-up.

Limitation dev has that this task fixes: dev's Tag button painted the untrusted tag text ("Tag: <tag>"). Since this task the button always reads `Tag`, and the tag is painted only by the literal border title (B2a), which `test_the_items_border_title_paints_the_tag_literally` covers.

_DESIGN_WIDTHS = {120: 24, 160: 35, 220: 50}


def _row_cells(fit: frame_state.ToolbarFit, mode: str) -> int:
    """The cells the controls take on their row: a gap and the label each."""
    return sum(
        frame_state.CONTROL_GAP_CELLS + cell_len(fit.labels[control])
        for control in frame_state.toolbar_controls(mode)
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sort_key", ["name_asc", "relevance", "modified_desc", "created_desc", "server"]
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", _MODES)
def test_the_toolbar_fits_one_row_at_160_and_two_at_120(mode, sort_key):
    """AC#1: at most 2 rows at 120 columns and 1 at 160 and wider, in every
    kind and with every sort label, and never a cut label: each one is its
    sort's full or short form. The search keeps at least 14 cells beside the
    controls (spec 1.5.1)."""
    forms = frame_state.SORT_LABELS[sort_key]
    assert set(frame_state.SORT_LABELS) == {
        "name_asc",
        "relevance",
        "modified_desc",
        "created_desc",
        frame_state.SERVER_SORT_KEY,
    }
    for columns, width in _DESIGN_WIDTHS.items():
        fit = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(mode, width=width, sort_key=sort_key)
        assert not fit.stacked, (columns, fit)
        assert fit.rows <= (2 if columns == 120 else 1), (columns, fit)
        assert set(fit.labels) == {
            "search",
            "import",
            *frame_state.toolbar_controls(mode),
        }
        if "sort" in fit.labels:
            assert fit.labels["sort"] in forms
        if fit.rows == 1:
            assert frame_state.TOOLBAR_SEARCH_MIN_CELLS + _row_cells(fit, mode) <= width
        else:
            assert _row_cells(fit, mode) <= width


def test_labels_shorten_before_the_toolbar_takes_a_second_row():
    """Spec 1.5.1: "labels shorten, never wrap". At 160 columns "Recent edit"
    does not fit beside a 14-cell search, so it reads "Edited" on one row."""
    narrow = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(
        "characters", width=35, sort_key="modified_desc"
    )
    wide = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(
        "characters", width=50, sort_key="modified_desc"
    )
    assert (narrow.rows, narrow.labels["sort"]) == (1, "Edited")
    assert (wide.rows, wide.labels["sort"]) == (1, "Recent edit")


def test_only_a_pane_too_narrow_for_one_row_of_controls_stacks_them():
    """80x24 (12 cells): Name, Tag and + New cannot share a row, so each takes
    its own and stays whole (TASK-33787 AC#4); two controls that fit share it."""
    fit = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar("characters", width=12, sort_key="name_asc")
    assert (fit.rows, fit.stacked) == (4, True)
    for control in frame_state.toolbar_controls("characters"):
        assert frame_state.CONTROL_GAP_CELLS + cell_len(fit.labels[control]) <= 12
    personas = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar("personas", width=12, sort_key="name_asc")
    assert (personas.rows, personas.stacked) == (2, False)


def test_the_rail_title_yields_to_import_below_about_100_columns():
    """Owner decision D2: "Library" shows beside the interim Import… where
    both fit whole (100 columns and wider), and yields below that."""
    shown = {
        width: frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(
            "characters", width=width, sort_key="name_asc"
        ).title
        for width in (12, 19, 20, 24)
    }
    assert shown == {12: False, 19: False, 20: True, 24: True}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", _MODES)
def test_the_search_placeholder_names_the_kind_and_carries_no_slash_hint(mode):
    """Owner decision D4: no "/" hint until frame slice B3 binds the key; the
    long form names the kind, and the fit falls back to "Search…" where the
    long one does not fit."""
    noun = frame_state.ITEM_KINDS[frame_state.KIND_FOR_MODE[mode]][1]
    assert frame_state.search_placeholder(mode, short=False) == f"Search {noun}…"
    assert frame_state.search_placeholder(mode, short=True) == "Search…"
    for width in (12, 24, 35, 50):
        fit = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(mode, width=width, sort_key="name_asc")
        assert "/" not in fit.labels["search"]
        search_cells = width if fit.rows > 1 else width - _row_cells(fit, mode)
        inside = search_cells - frame_state.SEARCH_CHROME_CELLS
        assert (
            cell_len(fit.labels["search"]) <= inside
            or fit.labels["search"] == "Search…"
        )


def test_the_toolbar_follows_the_ascii_glyph_mode(ascii_mode):
    """ASCII mode spells the ellipsis "...", so Import takes 9 cells: the fit
    measures the words it paints."""
    fit = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar("characters", width=20, sort_key="name_asc")
    assert fit.labels["import"] == "Import..."
    assert fit.labels["search"] == "Search..."
    assert fit.title is False  # 20 - 1 - 9 - 3 leaves 7 cells; "Library" needs 9


def test_the_sort_names_an_unknown_key_as_name_and_says_it_whole():
    """Dev labelled an unknown key "Sort: Name"; the tooltip carries the whole
    sort and the key, so a short label never hides which sort is on."""
    assert frame_state.sort_label("bogus") == "Name"
    assert frame_state.sort_label(frame_state.SERVER_SORT_KEY, short=True) == "Server"
    assert frame_state.sort_tooltip("modified_desc") == (
        "Sort: Recent edit. Click to change the order. (s)"
    )

def _painted_label(app, selector: str) -> str:
    """What the terminal shows inside one control's region."""
    region = app.query_one(selector).region
    return painted_rows(app.screen)[region.y][region.x : region.right]

@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [12, 24, 35, 50])
async def test_the_toolbar_paints_what_its_fit_chose(width):
    """The fit's cell constants mirror the lazy sheet: each control is exactly
    its label wide, one gap after the previous part, and the search spends
    SEARCH_CHROME_CELLS around its text. A CSS edit that forgets the
    constants fails here instead of clipping a control."""
    app = _StyledToolbarHost()
    async with app.run_test(size=(120, 36)) as pilot:
        pane = app.query_one(PersonasLibraryPane)
        pane.styles.width = width
        pane.set_mode("characters")
        await pilot.pause()
        await pilot.pause()
        fit = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(
            "characters", width=width, sort_key="name_asc"
        )
        toolbar = app.query_one("#personas-library-toolbar")
        search = app.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input)
        assert toolbar.region.height == fit.rows
        assert search.region.height == 1
        assert search.region.width - search.content_region.width == (
            frame_state.SEARCH_CHROME_CELLS
        )
        assert search.placeholder == fit.labels["search"]
        # On one row the first control follows the search box.
        previous = search.region if fit.rows == 1 else None
        for control in frame_state.toolbar_controls("characters"):
            selector = f"#personas-library-{control}"
            region = app.query_one(selector).region
            assert _painted_label(app, selector) == fit.labels[control]
            assert region.width == cell_len(fit.labels[control])
            if fit.stacked or previous is None:
                assert region.x == pane.content_region.x + frame_state.CONTROL_GAP_CELLS
            else:
                assert region.x == previous.right + frame_state.CONTROL_GAP_CELLS
            if not fit.stacked:
                previous = region
        if fit.rows == 1:
            assert search.region.width == width - _row_cells(fit, "characters")
        title = app.query_one("#personas-library-title")
        assert title.display is fit.title
        assert _painted_label(app, "#personas-library-import") == fit.labels["import"]

def _seed_every_kind(mock_app_instance, db) -> None:
    """One item per kind whose name starts "Cha", so a "Cha" search keeps rows
    in every kind (348 characters named "Character NNNN" come with ``db``)."""
    from tldw_chatbook.Character_Chat.world_book_manager import WorldBookManager

    WorldBookManager(db).create_world_book("Charted Isles")
    service, _calls = _persona_service(
        [
            {
                "id": "p-cha",
                "name": "Chaplain",
                "system_prompt": "Bless the voyage.",
                "created_at": "2026-10-01T00:00:00",
            }
        ]
    )
    mock_app_instance.character_persona_scope_service = service
    mock_app_instance.chat_dictionary_scope_service = _dictionary_service(
        ("Chat slang", 2)
    )


async def _show_kind(pilot, screen, mode: str) -> None:
    """Switch kind as a mode chip does, and wait for that kind's rows."""
    kind = frame_state.KIND_FOR_MODE[mode]
    await screen._apply_mode(mode)
    await wait_until(
        pilot,
        lambda: (
            bool(visible_item_ids(screen))
            and all(i.startswith(f"{kind}:") for i in visible_item_ids(screen))
        ),
        what=f"the {mode} rows",
    )
    await settle(pilot)


def _search_and_list(screen) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """(search height, search content rows, the list's top row)."""
    search = screen.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input)
    return (
        search.region.height,
        search.content_region.height,
        screen.query_one(RoleplayItemList).region.y,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "size", [(80, 24), (120, 36), (160, 45)], ids=["80x24", "120x36", "160x45"]
)
async def test_the_focused_search_shows_what_you_type_and_nothing_moves(
    size, mock_app_instance, volume_348
):
    """TASK-33787 AC#1-#3 and #5 in every kind: the search box is one row at
    rest, focused, typed in and left, it paints the typed query, and the list
    keeps its row throughout. On dev, focus stacked an Input:focus border onto
    the one-row box: two rows tall, no content row, the typed text invisible
    and the list one row lower (RP-009; B2b fixes it)."""
    _seed_every_kind(mock_app_instance, volume_348)
    async with open_styled_roleplay(
        "mock", mock_app_instance, size=size, character_db=volume_348
    ) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        search = screen.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input)
        item_list = screen.query_one(RoleplayItemList)
        for mode in _KINDS:
            await _show_kind(pilot, screen, mode)
            rest = _search_and_list(screen)
            search.focus()
            await settle(pilot)
            focused = _search_and_list(screen)
            await pilot.press(*"Cha")
            await wait_until(
                pilot,
                lambda: (
                    screen.state.search_query == "Cha"
                    and bool(visible_item_ids(screen))
                ),
                what=f"the {mode} search",
            )
            await settle(pilot)
            typed = _search_and_list(screen)
            painted = painted_text(screen, search.content_region)
            item_list.focus()
            await settle(pilot)
            left = _search_and_list(screen)
            assert rest == focused == typed == left, (mode, rest, focused, typed, left)
            assert rest[:2] == (1, 1), mode
            assert "Cha" in painted, (mode, painted)
            search.value = ""
            await wait_until(
                pilot, lambda: screen.state.search_query == "", what="cleared"
            )
            await settle(pilot)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "size",
    [(80, 24), (120, 36), (160, 45), (220, 55)],
    ids=["80x24", "120x36", "160x45", "220x55"],
)
async def test_every_toolbar_control_is_whole_and_inside_the_pane(
    size, mock_app_instance, volume_348
):
    """TASK-33787 AC#4 and B2b AC#1 in every kind: each control and the search
    box lie inside the pane with their whole label painted, the toolbar takes
    at most 2 rows at 120 columns and 1 at 160 and wider, and Import sits on
    the rail's title row (owner decision D2)."""
    _seed_every_kind(mock_app_instance, volume_348)
    async with open_styled_roleplay(
        "mock", mock_app_instance, size=size, character_db=volume_348
    ) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        pane = screen.query_one("#personas-library-pane")
        inside = pane.content_region
        for mode in _KINDS:
            await _show_kind(pilot, screen, mode)
            rows = painted_rows(screen)
            for selector in _TOOLBAR_PARTS:
                widget = screen.query_one(selector)
                if not widget.display:
                    continue
                region = widget.region
                assert region.area and inside.contains_region(region), (
                    mode,
                    selector,
                    region,
                    inside,
                )
                if selector != "#personas-library-search":
                    label = str(widget.label)
                    assert rows[region.y][region.x : region.right] == label, (
                        mode,
                        selector,
                    )
            toolbar = screen.query_one("#personas-library-toolbar")
            if size[0] >= 160:
                assert toolbar.region.height == 1, mode
            elif size[0] == 120:
                assert toolbar.region.height <= 2, mode
            header = pane.query_one(".console-rail-header")
            assert screen.query_one("#personas-library-import").region.y == (
                header.region.y
            )


async def test_the_server_runtime_toolbar_keeps_its_disabled_controls_whole(
    mock_app_instance,
):
    """Review Focus 5: under the server runtime + New and Tag are disabled but
    still take their cells, and the sort reads the server's order ("Server"
    beside a 14-cell search at 160 columns), so the row still fits whole."""
    records = [{"id": n, "name": f"Remote {n:03d}"} for n in range(1, 6)]

    async def list_characters(*, mode, limit, offset):
        return [dict(record) for record in records[offset : offset + limit]]

    mock_app_instance.runtime_backend = "server"
    mock_app_instance.active_server_id = "server-a"
    mock_app_instance.character_persona_scope_service = SimpleNamespace(
        list_characters=list_characters,
        search_characters=AsyncMock(return_value=[]),
        get_character=AsyncMock(return_value=dict(records[0])),
    )
    async with open_styled_roleplay("mock", mock_app_instance, size=(160, 45)) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        await wait_until(
            pilot, lambda: len(visible_item_ids(screen)) == 5, what="the server rows"
        )
        await settle(pilot)
        rows = painted_rows(screen)
        toolbar = screen.query_one("#personas-library-toolbar")
        assert toolbar.region.height == 1
        for part, label in (("sort", "Server"), ("tag", "Tag"), ("new", "+ New")):
            button = screen.query_one(f"#personas-library-{part}", Button)
            assert button.disabled is (part != "sort")
            region = button.region
            assert rows[region.y][region.x : region.right] == label
        sort = screen.query_one("#personas-library-sort", Button)
        assert str(sort.tooltip).startswith("Sort: Server order.")


async def test_a_resize_refits_the_toolbar_without_mounting(
    mock_app_instance, volume_348, work
):
    """Spec 2.13 "display-only layout": crossing 120 <-> 160 columns moves the
    controls between one row and two by classes and labels alone: 0 mounts,
    0 recomposes, no window read."""
    async with open_styled_roleplay(
        "mock", mock_app_instance, size=SIZE, character_db=volume_348
    ) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen

        def toolbar_rows() -> int:
            return screen.query_one("#personas-library-toolbar").region.height

        assert toolbar_rows() == 2
        for size, rows in (((160, 45), 1), ((120, 36), 2), ((160, 45), 1)):
            work.reset()
            work.armed = True
            await pilot.resize_terminal(*size)
            await settle(pilot)
            work.armed = False
            assert (work.mounts, work.recomposes) == (0, 0), size
            assert toolbar_rows() == rows, size
            assert work.windows == [], size

# ---- The items toolbar (frame slice B2b, spec 1.5.1; owner decision D2) ----

#: The search box never gets fewer cells than this (spec 1.5.1).
TOOLBAR_SEARCH_MIN_CELLS = 14
#: Cells the toolbar spends around its parts. They mirror the CSS:
#: ``Tests/UI/test_roleplay_item_list_app.py`` pins them against the mounted
#: widgets, so a CSS edit that forgets these fails there instead of clipping.
SEARCH_CHROME_CELLS = 3  # .settings-compact-input: border-left + padding 0 1
CONTROL_GAP_CELLS = 1  # .roleplay-items-control: margin-left $ds-space-1
RAIL_COLLAPSE_CELLS = 3  # .console-rail-collapse-button: width $ds-size-3
RAIL_TITLE_CHROME_CELLS = 2  # .personas-column-title: padding 0 1
#: The rail title, which yields to the interim Import (spec 5.3) when both
#: do not fit (below about 100 columns).
RAIL_TITLE = "Library"
#: The sort the server's own order shows under (it has no local key).
SERVER_SORT_KEY = "server"
#: Each sort's label, full and short (spec 1.5.1: labels shorten, never wrap).
SORT_LABELS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
    "relevance": ("Relevance", "Best"),
    "name_asc": ("Name", "Name"),
    "modified_desc": ("Recent edit", "Edited"),
    "created_desc": ("Recent add", "Added"),
    SERVER_SORT_KEY: ("Server order", "Server"),
}
#: The controls each kind's toolbar row shows, left to right (spec 1.5.1);
#: a mode without an items list keeps only ``+ New``.
TOOLBAR_CONTROLS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "characters": ("sort", "tag", "new"),
    "personas": ("sort", "new"),
    "lore": ("new",),
    "dictionaries": ("new",),
}


def toolbar_controls(mode: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The controls a mode's toolbar shows (``sort``, ``tag``, ``new``)."""
    return TOOLBAR_CONTROLS.get(mode, ("new",))


def sort_label(sort_key: str, *, short: bool = False) -> str:
    """The sort button's label; an unknown key reads as ``Name`` (as on dev)."""
    full, short_form = SORT_LABELS.get(sort_key, SORT_LABELS["name_asc"])
    return short_form if short else full


def sort_tooltip(sort_key: str) -> str:
    """The sort button's tooltip: the whole sort name and the key (``s``)."""
    return f"Sort: {sort_label(sort_key)}. Click to change the order. (s)"


def search_placeholder(mode: str, *, short: bool) -> str:
    """The search box's placeholder: ``Search characters…`` or ``Search…``.

    No ``/`` hint until frame slice B3 binds the key (owner decision D4).
    """
    ellipsis = resolve_glyph(_ELLIPSIS)
    kind = KIND_FOR_MODE.get(mode)
    if short or kind is None:
        return f"Search{ellipsis}"
    return f"Search {ITEM_KINDS[kind][1]}{ellipsis}"


def import_label() -> str:
    """The interim ``Import…`` on the rail's title row (spec 5.3; owner D2)."""
    return f"Import{resolve_glyph(_ELLIPSIS)}"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolbarFit:
    """How the items toolbar lays out at one width (spec 1.5.1).

    Attributes:
        rows: The toolbar's rows: 1 (the search beside the controls), 2 (the
            controls on the row under the search) or one more per control
            (stacked).
        labels: The words to paint, by part: the search placeholder
            (``search``), ``import`` and each shown control.
        stacked: Each control takes its own row (only where one row of
            controls does not fit: 80x24).
        title: The rail title shows beside ``Import…``.
    """

    rows: int
    labels: Mapping[str, str]
    stacked: bool
    title: bool


def fit_items_toolbar(mode: str, *, width: int, sort_key: str) -> ToolbarFit:
    """The toolbar's layout at ``width`` cells: a ladder, never a clipped label.

    One row with the full labels, then one row with the short ones, then two
    rows (full, then short), then every control on its own row. The search
    keeps at least ``TOOLBAR_SEARCH_MIN_CELLS`` beside the controls and shows
    its long placeholder only where it fits.

    Args:
        mode: The workbench mode (``toolbar_controls``).
        width: The pane's content width.
        sort_key: The list's sort (``SERVER_SORT_KEY`` for the server's order).

    Returns:
        The rows, the labels to paint, whether the controls stack, and
        whether the rail title shows.
    """
    controls = toolbar_controls(mode)

    def labels_for(short: bool) -> dict[str, str]:
        words = {
            "sort": sort_label(sort_key, short=short),
            "tag": "Tag",
            "new": "+ New",
        }
        return {control: words[control] for control in controls}

    def row_cells(labels: Mapping[str, str]) -> int:
        return sum(CONTROL_GAP_CELLS + cell_len(label) for label in labels.values())

    def placeholder(search_cells: int) -> str:
        full = search_placeholder(mode, short=False)
        fits = cell_len(full) <= search_cells - SEARCH_CHROME_CELLS
        return full if fits else search_placeholder(mode, short=True)

    import_words = import_label()
    beside_title = width - CONTROL_GAP_CELLS - cell_len(import_words)
    title = beside_title - RAIL_COLLAPSE_CELLS >= (
        cell_len(RAIL_TITLE) + RAIL_TITLE_CHROME_CELLS
    )

    def fit(
        rows: int, labels: dict[str, str], search_cells: int, stacked: bool
    ) -> ToolbarFit:
        words = {"search": placeholder(search_cells), "import": import_words}
        return ToolbarFit(rows, {**words, **labels}, stacked, title)

    full, short = labels_for(False), labels_for(True)
    for labels in (full, short):
        if TOOLBAR_SEARCH_MIN_CELLS + row_cells(labels) <= width:
            return fit(1, labels, width - row_cells(labels), False)
    for labels in (full, short):
        if row_cells(labels) <= width:
            return fit(2, labels, width, False)
    widest = max(CONTROL_GAP_CELLS + cell_len(label) for label in full.values())
    labels = full if widest <= width else short
    return fit(1 + len(controls), labels, width, True)
```

    def _required_toolbar_row_width(self) -> int:
        """Widest single-row width the currently visible bar buttons need.

        Derived from labels, not rendered sizes, so toggling the stacked
        class never changes the measurement (no layout oscillation).
        """
        required = 0
        for bar_id in ("#personas-library-toolbar", "#personas-library-filterbar"):
            row = 0
            for button in self.query(f"{bar_id} Button").results():
                if not button.display:
                    continue
                row += len(str(button.label)) + _TOOLBAR_BUTTON_CHROME_COLS
            required = max(required, row)
        return required

    def _sync_control_layout(self) -> None:
        """Stack the toolbar bars when one row would clip actions (F-030).

        A pane narrower than the single-row width clipped the rightmost
        buttons off-screen (at 100x30 that hid Import -- the roleplay
        onboarding path). Stacking switches each bar to a vertical layout so
        every action wraps onto its own row instead.
        """
        width = self.content_size.width
        if width <= 0:
            # Not laid out yet (on_mount); on_resize re-syncs once sized.
            return
        try:
            required = self._required_toolbar_row_width()
        except Exception:
            # Widths are label-derived, so a failure here is a teardown or
            # pre-compose race - but never something to swallow silently:
            # leaving the bars clipped with no trace was the bug under
            # review. Debug level, matching the teardown-race idiom used
            # across the personas widgets (the layout simply keeps its
            # previous state and re-syncs on the next resize).
            logger.opt(exception=True).debug(
                "PersonasLibraryPane toolbar width measurement failed; "
                "keeping the previous control layout."
            )
            return
        self.set_class(width < required, "personas-library-stacked-controls")

    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        """Compose the Library pane header, search controls, rows and marks bar.

    def _apply_toolbar_fit(self) -> None:
        """Lay the toolbar out for the pane's width (spec 1.5.1): display only.

        Two classes, the labels and one width per control; it mounts nothing,
        and a fit equal to the one applied does nothing at all, so a resize
        that keeps the fit costs one pure function call.
        """
        width = self.content_size.width
        if width <= 0:
            return  # not laid out yet (on_mount); on_resize fits it once sized
        fit = frame_state.fit_items_toolbar(
            self._mode, width=width, sort_key=self._sort_key
        )
        if fit == self._toolbar_fit:
            return
        self._toolbar_fit = fit
        self.query_one("#personas-library-toolbar", Horizontal).set_class(
            fit.rows > 1, "roleplay-items-toolbar-wrapped"
        )
        self.query_one("#personas-library-controls", Horizontal).set_class(
            fit.stacked, "roleplay-items-controls-stacked"
        )
        self.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input).placeholder = fit.labels[
            "search"
        ]
        self.query_one("#personas-library-title", Static).display = fit.title
        for part in ("import", "sort", "tag", "new"):
            label = fit.labels.get(part)
            if label is not None:
                button = self.query_one(f"#personas-library-{part}", Button)
                button.label = Content(label)
                # Exactly the label's cells, unpadded, as the marks bar's
                # actions: the controls' margin is the gap (Textual 8.2.8's
                # Button pads an auto width by two cells, and its CSS parser
                # refuses `line-pad: 0`).
                # ds-runtime: the cell width of the label this fit chose.
                button.styles.width = cell_len(label)
                button.styles.line_pad = 0

   label wide (an inline width), so the margin is the gap between them. */
.roleplay-items-toolbar {

    width: $ds-width-fill;
    height: auto;

    width: auto;
    height: auto;
}

}

### Task 8: The search placeholder and typed text at AA on every theme (RP-062, placeholder half; AC#13)

**Why.** On dev today the items search's placeholder is Textual's `$text-disabled`, which reads under 4.5:1 on all 89 measurable themes (2.12:1 on paradise_virtua, 3.54:1 at best on agentic_terminal), and a focused box paints nothing at all (RP-009, which Task 7 fixed). Both exist on dev, and B2b fixes both: AC#13 asks for the placeholder and the typed text at AA, at rest and focused, on every theme. Measured painted on Task 7's tree before this task, the dense form's focus fill also left the focused placeholder (`$text-disabled` on the focus fill, 2.42:1 on apricot) and, on five themes, the typed text under 4.5:1 (4.12:1 on catppuccin-frappe). That shortfall exists only on this branch, because on dev nothing painted focused; this task fixes it.

So, at rest, the placeholder takes `$ds-text-placeholder`. Focused, the box takes the house focus fill that `themes.py` guards for `$panel` (`$tldw-focus-fill`, the Workflows search's choice), Textual's 5% focus `background-tint` is dropped, and the placeholder takes the focus ink `$ds-focus-fg`. The rules are lazy: the Roleplay split claims Input's `input--placeholder` component class exactly, as B2a claimed OptionList's highlighted row, and `test_roleplay_stylesheet.py`'s `SHARED_CLAIMS` keeps every selector anchored by a Roleplay token. Boot CSS, the boot segment, the broad-selector count and the focus-edge census do not change (no new `border` or `outline` in a `:focus` rule).

Rulings the dry run made, each listed for the plan review:
- The focused box takes `$tldw-focus-fill` instead of the dense form's `$ds-input-focus-bg`, and drops the tint. Measured in four steps on the pane's real `$panel` fill: the token pair alone left 14 shortfalls (nord, catppuccin-mocha, -frappe and -macchiato, atom-one-dark focused, 4.12-4.49:1, plus 4 caret-cell reads); adding `background-tint: transparent` alone changed nothing (14); the focus fill brought it to 4 (all the caret cell over the first letter, because a programmatic value left the caret at 0); the test then puts the caret after the text, and it passes. The cost: the Roleplay search's focus fill differs from other dense-form inputs (its left edge is still theirs).
- **Owner decision D10 (2026-10-29), measured: the token stays.** D10 said to alias `$tldw-focus-fill` as a `$ds-` token in `css/core/_variables.tcss` only if that adds no boot CSS bytes. Dry-run on `b2b-draft-answers` at this task (2026-10-29): `$ds-focus-fill: $tldw-focus-fill;` (named for the `$ds-focus-*` family: `$ds-focus-bg`, `$ds-focus-fg`, `$ds-focus-accent`) in `_variables.tcss`, `.roleplay-items-search:focus` reading it, and the sheets rebuilt by `build_css.py`. `_boot_parsed_css_census()` (through `$EV/gates/boot_css.py`) read `boot-css=586881` on the parent and `boot-css=586916` with the alias: **+35 bytes**, because every split sheet, the boot bundle `tldw_cli_modular.tcss` among them, carries `_variables.tcss`'s declarations as its preamble (`build_css.py` strips the comment but not the one declaration line). So the alias was reverted, and the `$tldw-focus-fill` deviation stays (spec §2.12 item 5; Global Constraints). Both contrast tests passed with the alias in place (`90 passed, 2 warnings in 442.14s`, under load; the placeholder test and the 89 focus-edge themes), so the alias would change no colour, and again after the revert, at the head of `b2b-draft-answers` (`90 passed, 2 warnings in 638.09s`, load average 30). It is not taken only because D10 conditioned it on 0 boot bytes and it measured 35. (B2b's net boot change would still be −323 B with it, so no other gate decides this.)
- The painted host is the pane alone, with the workbench's id and class (its real `$panel` fill), not the whole screen. The focus fill is translucent over the pane, and 89 theme switches on the whole screen would cost minutes; no screen ancestor paints between the pane and the box.
- The caret is not measured: it is moved after the typed text and skipped on the placeholder's first cell, because AC#13 names the placeholder and the typed text. Limitation, exists on dev for every Input and not fixed by B2b: Textual's own caret colours over a letter measured 2.53:1 on pastel_dreams; the Workflows search restyles its caret, and Task 15 files the follow-up.
- The new test runs in `pr-fast-lane-admission-2`, beside the other painted contrast tests, with a `Tests/CI` contract pin. B2b already edits that workflow step for owner decision D7 (Task 4), so this adds no new manual-rebase exposure. If the owner prefers, the node can be dropped from the lane and run nightly only.

@pytest.mark.bootstrap_profile
@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_roleplay_items_search_placeholder_and_typed_text_clear_aa_on_every_theme() -> (
    None
):
    """Frame slice B2b AC#13 (RP-062), painted under the production
    stylesheets on every measurable theme: the search box's placeholder at
    rest, the placeholder with the box focused and the text typed into it
    each read at 4.5:1 on the fill they paint on. On dev the placeholder was
    Textual's $text-disabled, under 4.5:1 on all 89 measurable themes (2.12:1
    on paradise_virtua), and focused nothing painted at all (RP-009, a
    focused box with no content row)."""
    from textual.geometry import Region
    from textual.widgets import Input

    from Tests.UI.consolidated_css import APP_STYLESHEETS, ConsolidatedCSSApp
    from tldw_chatbook.Widgets.Persona_Widgets.personas_library_pane import (
        PersonasLibraryPane,
    )

    class Pane(ConsolidatedCSSApp):
        def compose(self):
            # The workbench's own id and class: the panel fill the focused
            # box's translucent focus fill composites over.
            yield PersonasLibraryPane(
                id="personas-library-pane", classes="destination-workbench-pane"
            )

    app = Pane(css_path=[str(path) for path in APP_STYLESHEETS])
    shortfalls: list[str] = []
    async with app.run_test(size=(80, 24)) as pilot:
        for theme in ALL_THEMES:
            app.register_theme(theme)
        app.query_one(PersonasLibraryPane).styles.width = 35
        search = app.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input)
        search.cursor_blink = False  # the caret is skipped, not read mid-blink
        for theme in MEASURABLE_THEMES:
            app.theme = theme.name
            app.set_focus(None)
            search.value = ""
            await pilot.pause()
            box = search.content_region
            read = {"placeholder at rest": _text_cells(app, box)}
            app.set_focus(search)
            await pilot.pause()
            # The caret paints on the placeholder's first cell.
            read["placeholder focused"] = _text_cells(
                app, box, [Region(box.x, box.y, 1, 1)]
            )
            search.value = "typed 123"
            # The caret after the text, on a blank cell: it paints Textual's
            # own cursor colours, which AC#13 does not cover (a programmatic
            # value can leave it on the first letter).
            search.cursor_position = len(search.value)
            await pilot.pause()
            read["typed text focused"] = _text_cells(app, box)
            for what, cells in read.items():
                if not cells:
                    shortfalls.append(f"{theme.name}: no {what} painted")
                for ink, fill in cells:
                    ratio = _ratio(ink, fill)
                    if ratio < AA:
                        shortfalls.append(
                            f"{theme.name}: {what} {ink} on {fill} is {ratio:.2f}:1"
                        )
    assert len(MEASURABLE_THEMES) >= 89
    assert not shortfalls, f"{len(shortfalls)} shortfalls:\n" + "\n".join(shortfalls)

### Task 9: Search-aware empty, no-match, loading and failure states (spec §1.5.4, RP-022, owner decisions D4 and D5; AC#3's message, AC#17, AC#24, AC#25, AC#27, AC#28)

**Why.** On dev today a search or tag filter that matches nothing makes every kind say "No <kind> yet - use New or Import to add one." over a library that holds items (TASK-33788), and the centre keeps "Pick a character from the list to see it here." over the empty list. A kind switch leaves the previous kind's rows and title up until the new kind's read lands, and Personas says "No personas yet" meanwhile. A failed character read says "No characters yet" under "Characters (?)", and the book kinds' failure copy says "Switch modes and back to retry." Escape in the list clears only the marks. All of this exists on dev, and this task fixes each one:
- A search or tag that empties a list says what found nothing, the kind's total and the way out: `No characters match "kepler".` and `28 in total · esc clears the search` (or `the tag`, or `the search and tag`). "No <kind> yet" shows only for a kind whose unfiltered total is 0, in the canonical nouns ("No chat dictionaries yet", OQ7), and it keeps the New/Import hint until frame slice B5b-2's kind empty state (OQ7).
- The no-match message is composed once and updated in place, so a keystroke that keeps the list empty mounts nothing (PERF-22).
- A kind switch blanks the old kind's rows at once and paints `Loading <kind>…` from a 250 ms timer (D5; one new timer, which Task 14's ADR-011 capture covers).
- A failed read shows the recovery row with a Retry button in every kind (D5; the first ever for characters), pinned for all four: `test_a_failed_character_read_shows_the_recovery_row_and_retry_reloads` and `test_retry_reloads_a_failed_list_in_every_kind[lore|dictionaries|personas]` (M9-H; plan review ruling 5).
- Escape in the list clears an active search and tag together before the marks (spec §4.5 rung 8, D4, ahead of frame slice B3). While the no-match message shows, Escape in the search box does the same (owner decision D9, 2026-10-29: rung 8 runs before the box's focus move), so the hint's "esc clears the search" is true where it is read: in the box, in the list and on an `Also in:` target. On dev the first Escape in the box moved focus to the list, so clearing from the box would have taken two presses; B2b changes that only while nothing matches. With rows listed, Escape in the box still moves focus to the list, as on dev (`test_escape_in_the_search_box_with_matches_moves_focus_to_the_list` is the control). Limitation, exists on dev and not changed by B2b: with a draft open, Escape cancels the draft first.
- With nothing open, the centre over an empty search reads the kind's line ("Characters — who the AI plays.", OQ8) and the truly-empty New/Import copy only when the unfiltered total is 0. The Inspector's "Pick a character or persona to start chatting." is left to B5b-2.

Limitation, exists on dev and not fixed by B2b: a mode chip's click runs the switch inside the screen's own message handler, so the screen repaints nothing until the read ends; the `c`/`p`/`d`/`l` keys, `Also in:` and the personas worker do paint the blank list and the loading line (probe P9-1 below). That is a deviation from D5 on the chip path: AC#17 is scoped to the worker-run switches, the PR body lists it, and Task 15 files the follow-up (run chip switches as workers; plan review ruling 5; Q6, accepted with the owner's agreement, 2026-10-29). Second limitation, exists on dev and not fixed by B2b: `Character_Chat_Lib`'s window-read wrappers swallow database errors (they return `[]` or 0), so a database fault inside them still reads as "no match", not as the failure row; Task 15 files it.

Rulings the dry run made, each listed for the plan review:
- `update_rows` loses `noun`: the copy's noun comes from the list's own kind through `ITEM_KINDS` (one owner, OQ7's canonical nouns). If wrong, a `noun` keyword comes back on 6 PS calls and 32 test calls.
- `update_rows` gains `query=` and `tag=` but not the outline's `unfiltered_total`: "N in total" is `total` whenever `filtered` (the border title's "of M" already), and is omitted otherwise (server characters, whose total is unknown: OQ14).
- The no-match block shows whenever a search or tag leaves no rows; the empty copy only with neither (TASK-33788 AC#2). A search in a kind that holds nothing reads `No lore books match "x".` / `0 in total · esc clears the search`.
- Copy: `No <kind> match "<q>".`, `No <kind> have the tag "<t>".`, `No <kind> match "<q>" with the tag "<t>".`; `<N> in total · esc clears the search|the tag|the search and tag`; the query and tag cut to one line of 24 cells (R33); `Loading <kind>…`; `Characters could not be loaded.`, `Dictionaries could not be loaded.`, `Lore books could not be loaded.` and `Retry` (tooltip "Read this list again."). The owner sees them in Task 14's captures.
- The book recovery copies drop "Switch modes and back to retry.": the Retry row replaces that advice.
- A blank server reload, a local read with no database and a server read that cannot start now end the wait with the failure row; on dev they showed "No characters yet" (blank) or kept the old rows (no database). Without this, "Loading characters…" would stay up forever: exists on dev in its "No characters yet" form, and B2b fixes it.
- Rung 8 runs with focus on the list or its marks bar (the marks' own condition). It clears search and tag together, keeps the selection and the marks, prevents `Input.Changed` and starts one render at once (no debounce, no second render). It also clears a search whose rows are still pending: it supersedes the find, and the owed landing drops through the fence. B3's rung 2 may later claim that state.
- The loading test drives the switch with the `l` key and polls on the event loop (`pilot.pause` waits for every pump): probe P9-1 measured that a mode chip's click blocks the screen's own message pump, so neither the blank nor the loading line paints until the read ends (`loading_display=True painted_loading=True painted_char=False app_q=2 screen_q=0` by key; `loading_display=True painted_loading=False screen_q=66` by chip).
- The loading timer's callback carries a serial, so a stopped timer's queued call says nothing (the PS debounce's lesson).
- `show_loading` is called in `_apply_mode` only after its synchronous lookups. The dry run first called it earlier and the textual worker contract flagged `1 new post-await DOM lookup(s)` in `_apply_mode`; Step 6 checks this.

def list_state(node) -> RoleplayListState:
    """The list's rows and cursor, and the copy shown beside it (spec 1.5.4)."""
    item_list = _item_list(node)
    items = tuple(item_at(node, index) for index in range(item_list.option_count))
    status = node.query_one("#personas-library-status")
    # Queried, not required: a tree without them reads as dev's states.
    loading = node.query("#personas-library-loading")
    state, text = "rows", None
    if status.display and status.children:
        static = status.children[0]
        text = str(static.render())
        state = "empty" if static.id == "personas-library-empty" else "recovery"
    elif no_match_lines(node):
        state, text = "no_match", "\n".join(no_match_lines(node))
    elif loading and loading.first().display:
        state, text = "loading", str(loading.first().render())
    return RoleplayListState(state, items, highlighted_item_id(node), text)


def no_match_lines(node) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The no-match message's painted lines (spec 1.5.4), or () while it is hidden."""
    blocks = node.query("#personas-library-nomatch")
    if not blocks or not blocks.first().display:
        return ()
    return tuple(
        str(line.render())
        for line in blocks.first().query(".personas-library-status-copy")
    )


def painted_option_rows(item_list: RoleplayItemList) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
    """The screen rows each option index is painted on (from the ``option`` style meta)."""
    region = item_list.content_region

def test_a_long_or_multiline_query_is_cut_to_one_line_literally(query):
    """The query is untrusted (R33): one line, at most 24 cells, as typed."""

def _status_lines(pane) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
    """Which status the pane shows beside its list, and its painted lines."""
    status = pane.query_one("#personas-library-status")
    no_match = pane.query_one("#personas-library-nomatch")
    if status.display and status.children:
        static = status.children[0]
        state = "empty" if static.id == "personas-library-empty" else "recovery"
        return state, (str(static.render()),)
    if no_match.display:
        return "no_match", tuple(
            str(line.render())
            for line in no_match.query(".personas-library-status-copy")
        )
    return "rows", ()

def _record_escapes(monkeypatch, gate: threading.Event) -> list[bool]:
    """Every Escape the screen handles, with whether the held read was released."""
    handled: list[bool] = []
    escape = PersonasScreen.action_personas_escape

def _record_spaces(monkeypatch, gate: threading.Event) -> list[bool]:
    """Every space the list handles, with whether the held read was released.

    Space on a character row does nothing, so it probes "a key is handled at
    once" without changing the find. B2a probed with Escape, which since
    frame slice B2b clears the active search from the list (spec 4.5 rung 8,
    owner decision D4) and so ends the find itself.
    """
    handled: list[bool] = []
    toggle = RoleplayItemList.action_toggle_highlighted

    def record(self) -> None:
        handled.append(gate.is_set())
        toggle(self)

    monkeypatch.setattr(RoleplayItemList, "action_toggle_highlighted", record)
    return handled


@pytest.mark.parametrize("debounce", ["pending", "fired"])

async def _search_settled(pilot, screen, query: str) -> None:
    """Type ``query`` into the search box and wait until its rows are in."""
    screen.query_one("#personas-library-search", Input).value = query
    await wait_until(
        pilot,
        lambda: (
            screen.state.search_query == query
            and not screen._search_rows_pending(screen._list_fence())
            and screen._search_debounce_timer is None
        ),
        what=f"the {query!r} search",
    )
    await settle(pilot)

async def _poll(predicate, what: str, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:
    """Wait on the event loop alone: ``pilot.pause`` waits for every message
    pump, and a kind switch's handler is still awaiting its read."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        if time.monotonic() > deadline:
            raise AssertionError(f"timed out after {timeout}s waiting for {what}")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.02)


async def test_loading_shows_only_after_250_ms_and_never_the_previous_kinds_rows(
    mock_app_instance, volume_348, monkeypatch
):
    """Spec 1.5.4 "Loading" (owner decision D5): a kind switch blanks the old
    kind's rows at once and paints "Loading lore books…" only from a 250 ms
    timer armed while it was still hidden. On dev the Characters rows and
    title stayed up until the lore read landed. The switch is the ``l`` key:
    a mode chip's click runs the switch inside the screen's own handler, so
    the screen paints nothing until the read ends (on dev too; not fixed)."""
    from tldw_chatbook.Character_Chat.world_book_manager import WorldBookManager

    WorldBookManager(volume_348).create_world_book("Kepler Atlas")
    reading, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    real_read = PersonasScreen._list_world_books_with_counts

    def held_read(manager):
        reading.set()
        release.wait(timeout=30)
        return real_read(manager)

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        PersonasScreen, "_list_world_books_with_counts", staticmethod(held_read)
    )
    armed: list[tuple[float, bool, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
    set_timer = PersonasLibraryPane.set_timer

    def spied_set_timer(self, delay, callback=None, **kwargs):
        loading = self.query_one("#personas-library-loading")
        armed.append((delay, loading.display, self.item_list.loaded_ids()))
        return set_timer(self, delay, callback, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(PersonasLibraryPane, "set_timer", spied_set_timer)
    async with open_styled_roleplay(
        "mock", mock_app_instance, size=SIZE, character_db=volume_348
    ) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        pane = screen.query_one("#personas-library-pane")
        screen.query_one(RoleplayItemList).focus()
        await settle(pilot)
        # The key's handler awaits the switch, so the press ends with the read.
        press = asyncio.create_task(pilot.press("l"))
        try:
            await _poll(reading.is_set, "the lore read")
            assert visible_item_ids(screen) == ()
            assert str(pane.border_title) == "Lore books (…)"
            await _poll(
                lambda: "Loading lore books…" in "\n".join(painted_rows(screen)),
                "the painted loading line",
            )
            assert list_state(screen).state == "loading"
            assert armed == [(0.25, False, ())]
            assert "Character 0" not in "\n".join(painted_rows(screen))
        finally:
            release.set()
            await press
        await wait_until(
            pilot, lambda: bool(visible_item_ids(screen)), what="the lore rows"
        )
        await settle(pilot)
        assert [item.name for item in list_state(screen).items] == ["Kepler Atlas"]
        assert list_state(screen).state == "rows"


async def test_a_failed_character_read_shows_the_recovery_row_and_retry_reloads(
    mock_app_instance, volume_348, monkeypatch
):
    """Spec 1.5.4 "Failure" (owner decision D5): a character read that fails
    shows the recovery row with Retry, and Retry reads the list again. On dev
    the list said "No characters yet - use New or Import to add one." under
    "Characters (?)", with no way back but a kind switch."""
    page = personas_screen_module.get_character_page_for_ui
    fail = {"on": False}

    def window(db, **kwargs):
        if fail["on"]:
            raise RuntimeError("disk I/O error")
        return page(db, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(personas_screen_module, "get_character_page_for_ui", window)
    async with open_styled_roleplay(
        "mock", mock_app_instance, size=SIZE, character_db=volume_348
    ) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        pane = screen.query_one("#personas-library-pane")
        fail["on"] = True
        await screen._reload_character_page()
        await settle(pilot)
        assert (list_state(screen).state, list_state(screen).text) == (
            "recovery",
            "Characters could not be loaded.",
        )
        retry = screen.query_one("#personas-library-retry", Button)
        assert str(pane.border_title) == "Characters (?)" and retry.display
        fail["on"] = False
        assert await pilot.click("#personas-library-retry")
        await wait_until(
            pilot,
            lambda: len(visible_item_ids(screen)) == 200,
            what="the reloaded rows",
        )
        await settle(pilot)
        assert list_state(screen).state == "rows" and not retry.display
        assert str(pane.border_title) == "Characters 349"


def _failing_read(mode: str, mock_app_instance, db, monkeypatch, fail: dict) -> str:
    """Make ``mode``'s list read raise while ``fail["on"]``; returns its one name."""
    if mode == "lore":
        from tldw_chatbook.Character_Chat.world_book_manager import WorldBookManager

        WorldBookManager(db).create_world_book("Kepler Atlas")
        real = PersonasScreen._list_world_books_with_counts

        def books(manager):
            if fail["on"]:
                raise RuntimeError("disk I/O error")
            return real(manager)

        monkeypatch.setattr(
            PersonasScreen, "_list_world_books_with_counts", staticmethod(books)
        )
        return "Kepler Atlas"
    if mode == "dictionaries":
        service = _dictionary_service(("Kepler slang", 2))
        listed = service.list_dictionaries

        async def dictionaries(**kwargs):
            if fail["on"]:
                raise RuntimeError("disk I/O error")
            return await listed(**kwargs)

        service.list_dictionaries = dictionaries
        mock_app_instance.chat_dictionary_scope_service = service
        return "Kepler slang"
    record = {
        "id": "p-kepler",
        "name": "Kepler Pilot",
        "system_prompt": "Fly the route.",
        "created_at": "2026-10-01T00:00:00",
    }
    service, _calls = _persona_service([record])
    listed = service.list_persona_profiles

    async def profiles(**kwargs):
        if fail["on"]:
            raise RuntimeError("disk I/O error")
        return await listed(**kwargs)

    service.list_persona_profiles = profiles
    mock_app_instance.character_persona_scope_service = service
    return "Kepler Pilot"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["lore", "dictionaries", "personas"])
async def test_retry_reloads_a_failed_list_in_every_kind(
    mock_app_instance, volume_348, monkeypatch, mode
):
    """Owner decision D5: a failed read shows the recovery row with Retry in
    every kind, not only Characters, and Retry reads that kind's list again.
    Dev had no Retry in any kind: its copy said to switch modes and back."""
    fail = {"on": True}
    name = _failing_read(mode, mock_app_instance, volume_348, monkeypatch, fail)
    async with open_styled_roleplay(
        "mock", mock_app_instance, size=SIZE, character_db=volume_348
    ) as pilot:
        screen = pilot.app.screen
        retry = screen.query_one("#personas-library-retry", Button)
        assert await pilot.click(f"#personas-mode-{mode}")
        await wait_until(pilot, lambda: retry.display, what="the Retry button")
        assert list_state(screen).state == "recovery"
        if mode == "personas":
            # The persona recovery row is dev's service-error copy.
            assert screen.query("#personas-service-error")
        fail["on"] = False
        assert await pilot.click("#personas-library-retry")
        await wait_until(
            pilot,
            lambda: [item.name for item in list_state(screen).items] == [name],
            what=f"the reloaded {mode} list",
        )
        await settle(pilot)
        assert list_state(screen).state == "rows" and not retry.display
        assert not screen.query("#personas-service-error")

# ---- Empty, no match, loading (frame slice B2b, spec 1.5.4) ----

#: ``Loading <kind>…`` shows only once a kind's read has taken this long.
LOADING_DELAY_SECONDS = 0.25
#: The echoed query or tag is cut to this many cells, on one line (R33).
NO_MATCH_ECHO_MAX_CELLS = 24


def empty_kind_text(kind: str) -> str:
    """The list's line when the kind holds nothing at all (its unfiltered total is 0).

    It keeps the New/Import hint until frame slice B5b-2's kind empty state
    takes the explanation (spec R25), in the canonical nouns.
    """
    return f"No {ITEM_KINDS[kind][1]} yet - use New or Import to add one."


def loading_text(kind: str) -> str:
    """``Loading characters…`` (spec 1.5.4)."""
    return f"Loading {ITEM_KINDS[kind][1]}{resolve_glyph(_ELLIPSIS)}"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NoMatchView:
    """What the list says when a search or tag leaves it empty (spec 1.5.4).

    Attributes:
        lines: What found nothing (``No characters match "kepler".``) and the
            way out (``28 in total · esc clears the search``). Plain text: the
            pane paints it with markup off (the query and tag are untrusted).
    """

    lines: tuple[str, str]


def no_match_view(
    kind: str, *, query: str, tag: str | None, total: int | None
) -> NoMatchView:
    """The no-match message for a search, a tag, or both (spec 1.5.4, RP-022).

    Args:
        kind: The list's entity kind (``ITEM_KINDS`` keys).
        query: The search as typed (cut to one line of
            ``NO_MATCH_ECHO_MAX_CELLS`` cells).
        tag: The active tag, if any (cut the same way).
        total: The kind's unfiltered total; None when it is unknown (a
            server search), which leaves ``N in total`` out.

    Returns:
        The two lines.
    """
    noun = ITEM_KINDS[kind][1]

    def echo(text: str) -> str:
        return ellipsize_cells(_one_line(text), NO_MATCH_ECHO_MAX_CELLS)

    if query and tag:
        found = f'No {noun} match "{echo(query)}" with the tag "{echo(tag)}".'
        cleared = "the search and tag"
    elif tag:
        found = f'No {noun} have the tag "{echo(tag)}".'
        cleared = "the tag"
    else:
        found = f'No {noun} match "{echo(query)}".'
        cleared = "the search"
    way_out = f"esc clears {cleared}"
    if total is not None:
        way_out = f"{total} in total {resolve_glyph(_SEPARATOR)} {way_out}"
    return NoMatchView((found, way_out))
```

    def _show_no_match(self, view: frame_state.NoMatchView | None) -> None:
        """Show or hide the no-match message; updated in place, never mounted."""
        if view is not None:
            for part, text in zip(("line", "hint"), view.lines):
                self.query_one(f"#personas-library-nomatch-{part}", Static).update(text)
        self.query_one("#personas-library-nomatch", Vertical).display = view is not None

    def no_match_showing(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the no-match message shows: a search or tag listed nothing."""
        return bool(self.query_one("#personas-library-nomatch", Vertical).display)

    def _show_retry(self, shown: bool) -> None:
        """Show Retry with the recovery copy; a hidden Retry hands its focus to the list (I1)."""
        retry = self.query_one("#personas-library-retry", Button)
        if not shown and retry.has_focus:
            self.item_list.focus()
        retry.display = shown

    async def show_loading(self) -> None:
        """A kind's first read started: blank the old kind's rows now, and say
        ``Loading <kind>…`` only if the read takes 250 ms (spec 1.5.4).

        On dev the previous kind's rows and title stayed up until the new
        kind's read landed, and Personas said "No personas yet" meanwhile.
        The next ``update_rows`` ends the wait.
        """
        self._stop_loading()
        self.item_list.show_rows((), kind_total=0)
        self._list_total = None
        self._filtered = False
        await self._sync_status(None)
        self._show_no_match(None)
        self._show_retry(False)
        self.set_title(frame_state.items_border_title(self.item_list.kind, total=None))
        serial = self._loading_serial
        self._loading_timer = self.set_timer(
            frame_state.LOADING_DELAY_SECONDS, lambda: self._loading_due(serial)
        )

    def _loading_due(self, serial: int) -> None:
        """The read is still running after the delay: say so (a stopped timer's late call says nothing)."""
        if serial != self._loading_serial:
            return
        self._loading_timer = None
        loading = self.query_one("#personas-library-loading", Static)
        loading.update(frame_state.loading_text(self.item_list.kind))
        loading.display = True

    def _stop_loading(self) -> None:
        """The wait ended (rows, an empty kind or a failure arrived)."""
        self._loading_serial += 1
        if self._loading_timer is not None:
            self._loading_timer.stop()
            self._loading_timer = None
        self.query_one("#personas-library-loading", Static).display = False

    def mark_active_row(
        self,
        kind: str,
